title: Reward-Hack Verbalization Mini-Suite in Toy Gameable Environments

original_idea.body: Reward-Hack Verbalization Mini-Suite. Problem: no small open reproducible suite of gameable toy tasks measures verbalization rate of an exploit for open models. Direction: design 3-4 toy tasks with an obvious shortcut, detect when the model uses it, check whether the CoT mentions it; report per-task use-rate vs verbalization-rate.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Compelling chain: open replication of silent reward-hack verbalization targets a pathway recognized as critical by major safety orgs.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing toy gameable tasks + shortcut detection; clear methodology.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 3-4 toy tasks; building several environments adds scope.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open reproducible suite labs ran only in proprietary envs; gold neglected external work.

novelty.reasoning: Verbalization gap shown in proprietary settings; open toy-suite replication may be partially open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The phenomenon is published; an open toy-environment verbalization suite is plausibly open.
